transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I'm here because I keep leaving my station at work. Or I'll just pop up during meetings when I'm supposed to stay put. My supervisor says it's becoming a real safety problem on the floor, because I just... I take off before I even think about it. So I guess that's why I'm here.
What is going through your mind or body right before you suddenly get up?

Well, it's mostly a physical feeling. Like, when I try to just stand still by my machine on the line, or if I have to sit through a training session, it feels like there's this... pressure building up inside my body. 

It just gets worse and worse until I feel like I absolutely have to move. I'll just need to pace, or stretch, or just go do something right then and there to let it out. I can't just ignore it.
When did you first start experiencing this urge to move?

Honestly, it's been going on pretty much my whole life. Like, even back in elementary school, I was always that kid who just couldn't stay in my seat. I'd talk over the teacher, and my mom was constantly getting notes sent home because I kept blurting things out or just... wandering around the room when I was supposed to be working. So yeah, it's always been like this.
Aside from needing to move around, do you also struggle with staying focused on tasks or details?

Yeah, I definitely do. Like, when I'm doing inventory logs at work, or reading the CNC training pages... I start out really trying to pay attention. But after just a few minutes, the numbers or the words just kind of blur together. I end up having to keep going back and re-reading the same thing because I realize I didn't actually take any of it in.
